# Vienna 1683 – Electricity & electronics

K = knowledge level · use = none/wrong/partial/correct · make = producibility with local means · accept = acceptance.

- **Static electricity, conductors and insulators, Leyden jar** [`static_electricity`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/static_electricity.md) — K2, use none, make medium, accept medium. Gilbert's 'electrics' and Guericke's rubbed sulphur globe (attraction, repulsion, crackling glow) are in print as curiosities. No conduction, no two kinds of charge, no storage jar. Local: apothecaries (sulphur, amber, resin); glassmakers; goldbeaters (foil); Guericke, Experimenta nova (1672), book IV. Elsewhere: Hamburg: Guericke; London: Boyle repeated the globe experiments (1672–1673).
- **Lightning rod** [`lightning_rod`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/lightning_rod.md) — K0, use none, make easy, accept low. Lightning is a sulphurous exhalation or God's hand; bells are rung against storms. A rod on a church invites the charge of tempting Providence. Any smith can make it. Local: spire of St Stephen's; powder magazines in the bastions.
- **Electric battery (voltaic pile)** [`electric_battery`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/electric_battery.md) — K0, use none, make hard, accept medium. Copper and silver are plentiful, but zinc metal is a rare East India import (tutenag, 'spelter') via Amsterdam. Brass is made with calamine, never with the metal. Local: mint and coppersmiths; brass founders (calamine); apothecaries (vitriol, salt).
- **Constant and rechargeable cells (Daniell, lead-acid, dry cell)** [`practical_batteries`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/practical_batteries.md) — K0, use none, make very-hard, accept medium
- **Electromagnetism and induction** [`electromagnetism`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/electromagnetism.md) — K0, use none, make hard, accept medium. Electric and magnetic attraction are held to be separate since Gilbert. Wire drawers supply copper and iron wire; silk for insulation is at hand. It waits on the battery.
